newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt signs four new oil/gas exploration deals.
newsitem.headline: Egypt signs four new oil/gas exploration deals.

text.p: Egypt has signed four agreements with foreign companies worth at least $39 million in investment to explore for oil and gas in the country's Western desert and Gulf of Suez, a Petroleum Ministry statement said on Monday.
It said the deals called for 14 exploratory wells.

Two of the deals were with the U.S. Pennzoil Co. In one, Pennzoil committed to invest at least $17 million and dig seven exploratory wells in West Beni Suef. The second in North July calls for $15 million investment for exploration and digging of three wells.
Spain's Repsol and U.S. Apache Corp signed an agreement to invest at least $1.75 million to dig a well in the East Umbarka area in the Western desert, the statement said.
An oil official added that South Korea's Samsung Corp., a Samsung Group unit, was also part of the deal.
Under the fourth agreement, the U.S. company USX Marathon will invest about $5.3 million for three wells in the West Gazwarina concession in the Gulf of Suez.
